name: 12. Chatbase migration, cutover & handover (Day 5)
description:
Part A · Day 5

Includes
Export chat history + leads from Chatbase; import into Supabase (pull the export on Day 1 — format is unknown until we have it, and finding out on cutover day is how this slips)
Cutover to the production number; update the WhatsApp link on the website
Short parallel run under live traffic before cancelling Chatbase
Cancel Chatbase only after the client confirms the new stack answers correctly
Attach the old number to the same WABA so it routes to the same bot
Handover: all credentials, tokens and connection strings in writing
Documentation: how the workflow is wired, how to read the error log, how to add a number
Walkthrough call with the client

Ownership check: Meta app, Supabase project, Render service and n8n workflows must all end up under the client's accounts. The dev Facebook account is for the sandbox only — the production app belongs in their Business Manager.

Done when
Bot answers on WhatsApp with Chatbase fully removed
Any conversation visible in the viewer within a minute
Monthly cost = OpenAI + n8n + hosting only

name: 11. Deploy to Render + keep-alive (Day 5)
description:
Part A + B · Day 5 — only after task 10 passes locally

Steps
Connect the GitHub repo in Render → New Web Service
Runtime Python 3.11. Build: pip install -r requirements.txt. Start: uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT
Add every variable from .env.example in the Render dashboard; set APP_BASE_URL to the Render URL
Health check path /health
Update the Meta callback URL to https://<service>.onrender.com/webhook/whatsapp and re-verify
Live test message — full round trip

⚠️ Free-plan constraint. Render spins a free web service down after 15 minutes without inbound traffic, and spin-up takes ~1 minute. Since our app receives the Meta webhook, a sleeping service delays or drops the first message after a quiet period.

Mitigations
External cron (cron-job.org / UptimeRobot) hitting /health every 10 minutes. One always-on service fits inside the 750 free instance-hours/month but consumes essentially all of them — keep to a single free service in the workspace
wa_message_id dedup (task 4) is what prevents cold starts causing duplicate replies
Recommend the paid instance before client cutover. Raise it before the first missed message, not after

Do NOT use Render's free Postgres — it expires 30 days after creation. Our database is Supabase; Render hosts the app only.

name: 10. End-to-end test locally on test number (Day 5)
description:
Part A + B · Day 5 — must pass before any deployment

Part A checklist
Webhook GET verification returns the challenge
Valid signature accepted, invalid rejected with 403
Ack under 300ms under load
Duplicate wa_message_id processed exactly once
Inbound logged with correct contact + conversation
n8n API receives payload and returns a reply
Reply reaches the customer's phone
Outbound logged with Meta message ID
New conversation opens after a 24h gap
n8n stopped → fallback sent, error logged
Invalid Meta token → error logged with Meta's code
Non-text message (image, voice) recorded by type, no crash

Part B checklist
Unauthenticated access redirects to login
Conversations newest first, counts and times correct
Thread renders in order, correct sides
Phone-number search returns the right thread
Keyword search matches bodies
Date filter works alone and with search
Leads unique, no duplicates
CSV + XLSX open cleanly in Excel
New message visible in viewer within 60 seconds
Error log page lists a forced failure
Timestamps display in Asia/Karachi

name: 9. Search, leads, export & error log page (Day 4)
description:
Part B · Day 4

Includes
GET /search — by phone number, and keyword across message bodies using the GIN full-text index
Date filter (from/to), combinable with search
GET /leads — unique contacts: number, name, first contact, last contact, message count
GET /export/leads.csv and .xlsx — streams the current filtered result set, not everything
GET /errors — recent error_log rows (step, message, time) for warranty-period support
Simple user management page — create/disable viewer logins

Done when
Keyword search matches message bodies
Date filter works alone and combined with search
Leads view shows unique contacts, no duplicates
CSV and XLSX both open cleanly in Excel

name: 8. Auth & viewer core — conversations + thread (Day 4)
description:
Part B · Day 4

Password-protected web viewer. Server-rendered Jinja2, plain CSS, no build step, no CDN dependencies.

Includes
GET/POST /login, /logout — sessions against app_users
Password hashing argon2 or bcrypt; rate-limit /login
Cookies HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax
GET /conversations — newest first: number, WhatsApp name, last message time, message count. Paginated 50/page
GET /conversations/{id} — full thread, WhatsApp-style bubbles: customer left, bot right, timestamps, day separators
Timestamps displayed in Asia/Karachi

Done when
Unauthenticated access redirects to login
List ordered correctly with accurate counts
Thread renders in order with correct sides

Read-only: no reply box, no send-message endpoint for humans. Explicit client scope — do not add one.

name: 7. Meta send & error handling / fallback (Day 3)
description:
Part A · Day 3

Send the reply through the Cloud API, and guarantee no silent failures.

Includes
meta_client.py — POST /{phone_number_id}/messages, pinned META_API_VERSION
Retry twice on send failure; store Meta's error code, not just the message
Write every failure to error_log with step (webhook/n8n/meta_send/db)
Fallback reply — customer always gets a graceful message, never silence. Reads like a person: "Sorry, I'm having trouble answering right now. Please try again in a moment."
60s watchdog — if no n8n callback arrives, log the timeout and send the fallback
Fallbacks are logged as outbound messages so they appear in the viewer thread
DB unreachable must never block a customer reply — log to stdout so Render captures it

Done when
n8n stopped → customer receives fallback, error logged
Invalid Meta token → error logged with Meta's code
No path exists where a customer message gets no response at all

name: 6. Connect n8n API for bot replies (Day 3)
description:
Part A · Day 3 — the core integration

The bot is already built and trained in n8n. We are not rebuilding it. This task connects our application to the n8n API so the trained bot's reply reaches WhatsApp.

App → n8n (POST {N8N_WEBHOOK_URL})
{
  "conversation_id": 4812,
  "wa_id": "923001234567",
  "profile_name": "Ahmed",
  "message": "Do you deliver to Lahore?",
  "message_id": "wamid.HBgM...",
  "callback_url": "https://<app>/internal/reply"
}
No prompt, no model settings, no knowledge sources in this payload — n8n owns all of it.

n8n → App (POST /internal/reply, header X-Callback-Secret)
{ "conversation_id": 4812, "wa_id": "923001234567", "text": "...", "status": "ok" }

Includes
n8n_client.py dispatch with 3× retry, exponential backoff (2s/4s/8s)
/internal/reply endpoint guarded by N8N_CALLBACK_SECRET, constant-time compare
Callback pattern, not a synchronous call — OpenAI latency is unbounded and a blocked worker produces duplicate replies

⚠️ BLOCKER — settle on Day 1, in writing. Confirm with whoever owns the workflow: (1) production webhook URL, (2) whether it accepts our field names or needs a mapping node, (3) whether memory keys on conversation_id or wa_id. Getting this wrong is the most likely cause of a lost day.

name: 5. Message logging & conversation windowing (Day 2)
description:
Part A + B · Day 2

Persist every message in both directions. This is the foundation of the whole viewer.

Includes
Contact upsert on wa_id; update profile_name, last_seen_at, message_count
24-hour conversation windowing: if the contact's latest conversation has last_message_at within 24h, append to it; otherwise open a new conversation row. Keep the 24h constant in config.py, not scattered through the code
Inbound persistence: direction customer, Meta timestamp, message type
Outbound persistence: direction bot, Meta message ID from the send response
Maintain message_count and last_message_at counters

Done when
Inbound message appears in messages with correct contact + conversation
A message after a 24h gap opens a new conversation
All timestamps stored UTC (timestamptz)

name: 4. Webhook receiver — verify, HMAC, dedup, fast ack (Day 1)
description:
Part A · Day 1

The app — not n8n — receives the Meta webhook.

Includes
GET /webhook/whatsapp — compare hub.verify_token, return hub.challenge as plain text, else 403
POST /webhook/whatsapp — verify X-Hub-Signature-256 HMAC-SHA256 over the raw request body (before any JSON parsing — re-serialised JSON will not match), constant-time compare
De-duplicate on wa_message_id: duplicates return 200 and do nothing
Schedule background work, return 200 immediately — target under 300ms
Parse text and non-text messages (image, voice) without crashing

Done when
Valid signature accepted, invalid rejected with 403
Ack under 300ms under load
Meta retry of the same message is processed exactly once

Why it matters: idempotency here is what stops a Render cold start turning into duplicate replies to a real customer.

name: 3. Meta app setup on dev Facebook account (Day 1)
description:
Part A · Day 1 — start this first, it is the longest external dependency

Steps
developers.facebook.com → create app, type Business
Add the WhatsApp product (provisions a test number + sandbox WABA)
Record Phone number ID and WABA ID
Business Settings → create a System User, assign the WABA as an asset, generate a permanent token with whatsapp_business_messaging + whatsapp_business_management (the dashboard token expires in 24h — do not rely on it)
WhatsApp → Configuration: set Callback URL to {tunnel}/webhook/whatsapp and the Verify token
Subscribe the webhook to the messages field — without this, verification goes green and no messages ever arrive
Add each developer's personal WhatsApp number as an approved test recipient

Done when
Webhook verification succeeds
A message sent from an approved number reaches our local endpoint

Note: the production app must ultimately live in the client's Business Manager (ownership clause in the proposal). Dev account is for the sandbox only.

name: 2. Supabase schema & migrations (Day 1)
description:
Part A + B · Day 1

Create the Postgres schema in Supabase.

Tables
contacts — wa_id (unique), profile_name, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, message_count
conversations — contact_id, started_at, last_message_at, message_count
messages — conversation_id, contact_id, wa_message_id (unique), direction ('customer'/'bot'), body, msg_type, media_url, sent_at, meta_status
error_log — conversation_id, wa_id, inbound_body, step, error_text, payload jsonb
app_users — email, password_hash (argon2/bcrypt), role, last_login_at

NOTE: no bot_config and no knowledge_sources table. The bot is trained in n8n and n8n owns its prompt, model and sources.

Indexes
messages (conversation_id, sent_at desc), messages (contact_id, sent_at desc)
conversations (last_message_at desc)
GIN full-text on to_tsvector('english', body) — required for keyword search
error_log (created_at desc)

Done when
migrations/001_init.sql runs clean in the Supabase SQL editor
Seed script creates the first admin user
App connects from local via DATABASE_URL

name: 1. Repo & FastAPI skeleton (Day 1)
description:
Part A · Day 1

Set up the GitHub repo so anyone can clone it and run the project locally without asking for missing pieces.

Includes
Repo structure: app/ (routers, services, db, templates, static), migrations/, tests/
FastAPI app + Uvicorn, router registration
app/config.py — Pydantic Settings for all env vars, fails fast if any required var is missing
GET /health returning 200 + DB ping
README.md with full local setup (clone → venv → install → .env → migrate → run → tunnel)
.env.example with every variable, placeholder values, committed
.gitignore must include .env

Done when
Clean clone + README steps → app runs locally on port 8000
/health returns 200
No secrets anywhere in the repo
